payload.title: a small judge model misreads a route as spec
payload.body: Assaying purview-guard-precise at 11799c43, the purview guard was run through its host-model seam against live models, five samples per act. With the session's default model, 35 of 35 architect acts were judged right: four routes (build it, assay it, findings back to a running agent, a closed plan to the integrator) and a shard to a planner passed, and a spec to an implementer and a source write were denied. With the smaller 'smol' model, the route 'purview-guard-precise of guard-precision: build it.' to an implementer and the findings-back message were denied 5 of 5 as spec, although the rubric names 'build it' as a route event. The rubric before the unit (6.6 KB, at cbac6a5f) gave the same two denials under that model, and it also denied the shard to a planner 3 times in 5, which the new rubric passes 5 of 5. So the concise hand did not cause this; the residual is judge-model capacity. The deployed Claude Code judge is haiku, and it could not be exercised here because the claude CLI hung headless. Whether the guard's judge model is strong enough to tell a route from a spec is open.
